title: the DSG equipment descriptions

banner.title: The DSG NEW EQUIPMENT DESCRIPTIONS AND TRANSPORTATION, R526: printed pp. 56-57 (pdf 57-58) - the item descriptions: the air bladder (an airtight leather sack, flotation at a 1/3 kick rate with no exertion or swimming needed, hypothermia still a danger, and a full turn of rest air rising at the air-supply proportions when exerting), the baskets (woven, lidded, not waterproof), the beacon (a mounted very-bright lantern throwing a 240-foot cone two feet wide at the source broadening to a 90-foot fan, a pint of oil per 10 turns, tightly shutterable), the birdcage (a wicker cage for up to three songbirds, 18 inches high and a foot in diameter), the boxes (small metal boxes about 2 x 2 feet and 1 1/2 inches deep, lightproof and airtight when sealed, foiling magical inspection and holding light-enchanted objects), the crampons (boot spikes for ice and slippery surfaces), the iron drill (a one-inch-wide, up-to-nine-inch-deep hole, one inch of wood per turn and stone in three, the grinding noise audible at 120 feet), the grappling hooks (two- or three-pronged, nearly always rope-attached), the waterproof lantern (a shielded flame; underwater a 10-foot radius instead of 30, the flame surviving the water but not the missing air - a secret d6 of remaining rounds), the lard pint (a lubricant squeezing a character through a passage 80% of the minimum, too stubborn to burn as a weapon but adding 2 hp per round of fire damage for 1d6 rounds, and an insulating coating per the hypothermia rules), the waterproofing oil (seal- and mink-harvested, a pint coating two square yards of leather or wool but never cotton, repelling pouring water 1d6 x 6 turns, immersion 1d6 turns, then wetter for 1d6 turns until saturated), the pickaxe (the miner's essential, the excavation rate halved without it; a desperate weapon at an inherent -2 dealing 1d10 to small/medium and 1d20 to large creatures), the chalk powder (imagination-limited: floor footprints, a 10-foot dust cloud revealing invisible creatures, covering a 20-foot square or eight humans), the pulleys (one, two or three rope loops; two single pulleys double the lift, two double quadruple it, two triple sextuple it), the hollow reed (submerged breathing periscope-style, 1/3 movement with a 10% per-round ripple risk while moving, none while floating), the shovel (daily excavation halved without one) and the whistle (piercing, audible at 1,000 feet); and the transportation equipment: the collapsible boat (a skin-and-spar package filling a backpack, unfolding into a small-rowboat equivalent in 1d3 turns, twice the listed weight when carried wet), the canoe (swifter and more maneuverable than a rowboat but easier to capsize, carrying three characters with normal gear or two with heavy gear; the large canoe nine or six), and the kayak (a one-character craft for rough or cold water, the oilskin layer sealing everything but the kayaker's opening so even capsizing does not fill it)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~7255-7470) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 133 = the printed p. 57 window); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the beacon 240/2/90 cone and 10-turn pint, the drill 1x9 hole with the wood-per-turn and three-turn stone, the 120-ft noise, the lantern 10/30 radii with the d6 burn, the lard 80% passage and 2-hp 1d6 fire, the oil 2-sq-yd pint with the 1d6x6 pour, 1d6 immersion and 1d6 wetting, the pickaxe 50% rate, -2, 1d10/1d20, the chalk 20-ft square/8/10-ft cloud, the reed 1/3 and 10% ripple, the 50% shovel rate, the 1,000-ft whistle, the 1d3-turn unfold with the doubled wet weight, and the canoe 3/2/9/6 crews. The only garbles are the standing glyph classes (djvu "809/" reading as 80%, the box depth "1 1/2" glyph). SEAMS: the air-supply page-36 and hypothermia page-42 references (R515/R516), the movement-rules page-21 passage width, the R520 pickaxe-and-shovel excavation rates, and the climbing rules for crampons and grappling hooks. The Equipment-for-Proficiencies descriptions prose (the armorer through weaver paragraphs) sits after the transportation section and lands with the next chapter block; nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention: the beacon cone (240/2/90 ft, 10 turns per pint), the birdcage (18 in, 12 in, 3 birds), the box (2x2 ft, 1 1/2 in deep), the drill (1-in x 9-in hole, 1-in wood per turn, stone in 3, 120-ft noise), the lantern (10/30-ft radii, the secret d6 burn), the lard (80% passage, 2 hp, 1d6 rounds), the oil (2 sq yd, 1d6 x 6 pour, 1d6 immersion, 1d6 wetting), the pickaxe (50% rate, -2 attack, 1d10/1d20), the chalk (400 sq ft, 8 creatures, 10-ft cloud), the reed (1/3 movement, 10% ripple), the shovel (50% rate), the whistle (1,000 ft), the pulleys (2x/4x/6x), and the transportation numbers (1d3 unfold, 2x wet weight, canoe 3/2 and 9/6 crews). The rest pins as prose bools: the item purposes and caveats (the bladder flotation and air-supply roles, the beacon mounting and shutter, the lightproof boxes, the shielded lantern dousing by missing air, the lard lubricant/insulator double life, the oil sources, the pickaxe miner's-kit role, the chalk discovery uses, the pulley loop ladder, the reed periscope and ripple, the sealed kayak). The R515/R516/R520/page-21 seams are noted; nothing auto-credits.

prev_record: - R525 LANDED 2026-10-17: commit 9cf5b25 (census 448 -> 449,
pushed 7c7074c..9cf5b25), THE DSG EQUIPMENT COSTS AND
WEIGHTS, printed pp. 56-57 (pdf 57-58) - the chapter frame
(the equipment primarily for underground exploration but
usable in any AD&D campaign, listed with average cost and
typical encumbrance, the specific uses tied to the
climbing, mining and water-travel rules) and the Table 35
cost/weight grid: twenty general rows (air bladder 15 gp
and 20 gp, basket large 5 sp and 80 gp, basket small 2 sp
and 40 gp, beacon 40 gp and 200 gp, birdcage 5 sp and
50 gp, box small gold 100 gp and 20 gp, box small lead
20 gp and 20 gp, crampons 40 gp and 50 gp, crowbar 3 gp
and 75 gp, drill iron 5 gp and 50 gp, grappling hook
75 gp and 75 gp, lantern waterproof 50 gp and 50 gp, lard
pint 5 cp and 20 gp, oil waterproofing 1 gp and 20 gp,
pickaxe 20 gp and 200 gp, powder chalk 2 sp and 20 gp,
pulley 25 gp and 60 gp, reed hollow 1 sp and 1 pc, shovel
10 gp and 180 gp, whistle 1 sp and 1 pc) plus four
transportation rows (boat collapsible 500 gp and 600 gp,
canoe small 100 gp and 800 gp, canoe large 300 gp and
1,600 gp, kayak 250 gp and 500 gp); and the proficiency
equipment: the fourteen initial costs and minimum spaces
(animal trainer 100 gp and 1-20 acres, armorer 1,250 gp
and 20 x 20, blacksmith 1,000 gp and 30 x 30, boatwright
1,000 gp and 50 x 120, bowyer/fletcher 250 gp and 20 x
20, carpenter 400 gp and varies, gem cutter 2,225 gp and
15 x 15, leatherworker 300 gp and 15 x 15, miner 750 gp
and varies, potter 600 gp and 20 x 30, smelter 2,000 gp
and 50 x 50, stonemason 250 gp and varies, weaponsmith
1,500 gp and 40 x 30, weaver 500 gp and 30 x 30), the
space-required rule (undersized space = only partially
effective), and the raw-materials exclusion (the 11-20% -
1d10 + 10 - of finished work value, the armorer or
blacksmith needing iron and forge fuel). THE THIRD
OCR-FAILURE ROUND OF THE STRETCH: both machine reads
failed the same cells with genuine conflicts between them
(the djvu garbling every sp as the Cyrillic ар and
dropping the basket-small cost, the Capture layer
dropping the lard/reed/whistle cells), and the vision
passes wobbled the currency units - settled by Curtiss
reading the physical printed p. 56 (air bladder 15 gp -
the direct read that broke the unsafe sp-pattern
assumption - baskets, crowbar, pulley, reed and whistle).
The reed/whistle weight prints 1 pc - pinned as printed
per the never-repair rule. LESSONS: (1) the authoring
audit mirror caught a wrong-row lard index in a table
check before anything landed - the mirror evaluates, not
just counts; (2) the first user-side landing hit a NEW
failure class - ./bn delivered the spec with two stray
bytes appended after the closing brace (23257 vs 23255,
JSON 'Extra data'), diagnosed via wc -c + tail and fixed
with truncate -s 23255 - the md5-vs-authored check caught
it before the engine ran. Pinned as rules/dsgequip.h
(prefix dnta, verified free; 17 inlines - 5 consts, 8
bools, 4 table cols; Table 35 as a 24x2 grid normalized to
copper-piece costs and gp coin weights, the proficiencies
as a 14x2 grid with the -99 sentinel holding the acres and
Varies rows). Spec 23,255 bytes, md5
7afc57d1e1cf5d0e6345980787b306cc. Engine applied 7 then
0/7. Gap 121/34 -> 124/31 (3 flips: children 137, 140 and
the Table 35 manifest line 200). NEXT - R526: the new
equipment descriptions and transportation equipment
(printed pp. 56-57, pdf 57-58; children 138-139) - the
item prose (air bladder, baskets, beacon, birdcage, boxes,
crampons, drill, grappling hooks, waterproof lantern, lard,
waterproofing oil, pickaxe, chalk powder, pulleys, reed,
shovel, whistle) with their numbers (the beacon 240-ft
cone, the drill noise at 120 ft, the lantern 10-ft
underwater radius and secret d6 burn, the lard 80%
passage, the chalk 20-ft square, the pickaxe 1d10/1d20
damage, the whistle 1,000 ft), then the collapsible boat,
canoes and kayak, plus the animal-trainer proficiency
opener; djvu ~lines 7255-7420 already extracted and CLEAN
in both reads - a fast round expected. The descriptions
prose is extracted; verify children 138-139 exact wording.

consts.name: dnetBladderKickDiv
consts.comment: by kicking, a character holding an air bladder moves at 1/3 of his normal swimming speed.

consts.name: dnetBladderRestTurns
consts.comment: a resting character with an air bladder gets enough air to last a full turn (10 rounds).

consts.name: dnetBeaconRangeFt
consts.comment: a beacon projects light in a cone up to 240 feet from its source.

consts.name: dnetBeaconSourceWidFt
consts.comment: the beacon cone is only two feet wide at its source.

consts.name: dnetBeaconEndWidFt
consts.comment: the beacon cone broadens into a 90-foot-wide fan at its extreme end.

consts.name: dnetBeaconOilTurns
consts.comment: a beacon burns a pint of oil in 10 turns of operation.

consts.name: dnetBirdcageHeightIn
consts.comment: a birdcage is about 18 inches high.

consts.name: dnetBirdcageDiaIn
consts.comment: a birdcage is about one foot (12 inches) in diameter.

consts.name: dnetBirdcageBirds
consts.comment: a birdcage is capable of holding up to three songbirds.

consts.name: dnetBoxWidFt
consts.comment: the boxes are about two feet wide.

consts.name: dnetBoxLenFt
consts.comment: the boxes are about two feet long.

consts.name: dnetBoxDeepIn
consts.comment: the boxes are about 1 1/2 inches deep (the "1 1/2" glyph garbles in both machine reads - pinned by the R521-style small-measure convention, 18 half-inches).

consts.name: dnetDrillHoleWidthIn
consts.comment: the drill bores a hole about one inch wide.

consts.name: dnetDrillHoleDepthIn
consts.comment: the drill bores up to nine inches deep.

consts.name: dnetDrillWoodInPerTurn
consts.comment: a heavily exerting character drills through one inch of wood in a turn.

consts.name: dnetDrillStoneInPerTurnFrac
consts.comment: one inch of stone takes three turns.

consts.name: dnetDrillNoiseFt
consts.comment: the drill makes a grinding noise audible up to 120 feet away.

consts.name: dnetLanternUwRadiusFt
consts.comment: a waterproof lantern taken underwater illuminates a 10-foot radius.

consts.name: dnetLanternNormRadiusFt
consts.comment: the normal (dry) lantern radius is 30 feet.

consts.name: dnetLanternBurnDice
consts.comment: the submerged-lantern burn roll is one die, made secretly by the DM.

consts.name: dnetLanternBurnSides
consts.comment: a submerged waterproof lantern burns d6 rounds - the secret roll result.

consts.name: dnetLardPassagePct
consts.comment: a lard-smeared character can squeeze through a passage only 80% as wide as the minimum passage needed (the movement-rules page-21 seam).

consts.name: dnetLardExtraHp
consts.comment: a lard-smeared character sustaining fire-based damage suffers 2 hp extra per round.

consts.name: dnetLardExtraDice
consts.comment: the extra-damage duration is one die.

consts.name: dnetLardExtraSides
consts.comment: the fire extra damage lasts 1d6 rounds.

consts.name: dnetOilSqYards
consts.comment: one pint of waterproofing oil thoroughly coats two square yards of leather or wool.

consts.name: dnetOilPourDice
consts.comment: the pouring-water waterproof duration is one die.

consts.name: dnetOilPourSides
consts.comment: treated material repels pouring or showering water for 1d6 x 6 turns.

consts.name: dnetOilPourMult
consts.comment: the pour duration multiplies the 1d6 result by 6.

consts.name: dnetOilImmerseDice
consts.comment: the immersion waterproof duration is one die.

consts.name: dnetOilImmerseSides
consts.comment: immersed material remains completely waterproof for only 1d6 turns.

consts.name: dnetOilWetDice
consts.comment: the slow-wetting leak duration is one die.

consts.name: dnetOilWetSides
consts.comment: a leaking material grows slowly wetter for 1d6 turns, after which it is completely saturated.

consts.name: dnetPickNoPickaxeRatePct
consts.comment: the excavation rate is only 1/2 of maximum without pickaxes (the R520 seam).

consts.name: dnetPickAtkPenalty
consts.comment: a pickaxe used as a weapon suffers an inherent -2 on all attack rolls.

consts.name: dnetPickDmgSidesSm
consts.comment: a pickaxe blow inflicts 1d10 points of damage to small or medium creatures.

consts.name: dnetPickDmgSidesLg
consts.comment: a pickaxe blow inflicts 1d20 points of damage against large creatures.

consts.name: dnetChalkFloorSqft
consts.comment: a container of chalk powder thoroughly covers a 20-foot-square (400 sq ft) section of floor.

consts.name: dnetChalkCreatures
consts.comment: a container holds enough chalk powder to cover up to eight human-sized characters.

consts.name: dnetChalkCloudDiaFt
consts.comment: hurled or smashed chalk creates a 10-foot-diameter cloud of dust.

consts.name: dnetReedMoveDiv
consts.comment: a reed-breathing character can move at only 1/3 of his normal swimming movement rate.

consts.name: dnetReedRipplePct
consts.comment: a character moving while breathing through a reed stands a 10% chance per round of creating a tell-tale ripple.

consts.name: dnetNoShovelRatePct
consts.comment: a group without shovels has its daily excavation amount reduced by 50% (the R520 seam).

consts.name: dnetWhistleRangeFt
consts.comment: a whistle creates a piercing sound audible up to 1,000 feet away.

consts.name: dnetPulleyDoubleLiftMult
consts.comment: two single-rope pulleys double the weight that can be lifted.

consts.name: dnetPulleyQuadLiftMult
consts.comment: two double-rope pulleys quadruple the lift.

consts.name: dnetPulleyTripleLiftMult
consts.comment: two triple-rope pulleys increase the lift six times.

consts.name: dnetBoatUnfoldDice
consts.comment: the collapsible-boat unfold roll is one die.

consts.name: dnetBoatUnfoldSides
consts.comment: the collapsible boat unfolds into a shallow boat (a small rowboat equivalent) in 1d3 turns.

consts.name: dnetBoatWetMult
consts.comment: a collapsible boat carried when wet weighs twice the listed amount.

consts.name: dnetCanoeNormalCrew
consts.comment: a canoe can carry three characters with normal gear.

consts.name: dnetCanoeHeavyCrew
consts.comment: a canoe can carry two characters with heavy gear.

consts.name: dnetCanoeLgNormalCrew
consts.comment: a large canoe can hold nine characters with normal gear.

consts.name: dnetCanoeLgHeavyCrew
consts.comment: a large canoe can hold six characters with heavy gear.

bools.name: dnetBladderFlotationAndAir
bools.comment: the air bladder is an airtight leather sack with two principal purposes: a flotation device and a very limited air supply container, generally with several straps for holding.

bools.name: dnetBladderNoSwimNeeded
bools.comment: a character holding an air bladder does not have to exert himself to remain afloat, nor does he need to be able to swim - though hypothermia can still endanger him (the R516 seam).

bools.name: dnetBladderAirSupply
bools.comment: the secondary function provides air to a character who might otherwise suffocate or drown: resting, a full turn of air; exerting, the consumption rate rises at the air-supply proportions (page 36, the R515 seam).

bools.name: dnetBasketsLatched
bools.comment: the woven baskets are not waterproof but hold most nonliquid substances; each comes with a lid that can be latched tightly.

bools.name: dnetBeaconMounted
bools.comment: a beacon is essentially a very bright lantern too large to be carried by hand - it must be mounted on a structure such as a building, wagon, or boat.

bools.name: dnetBeaconShuttered
bools.comment: a beacon can be tightly shuttered so as not to emit even a trace of light.

bools.name: dnetBirdcageWicker
bools.comment: the birdcage is a wicker cage for up to three songbirds.

bools.name: dnetBoxesLightproof
bools.comment: the small metal boxes are completely light proof and airtight when sealed - useful against magical inspection, and handy containers for gems or permanently light-enchanted objects.

bools.name: dnetCramponsIce
bools.comment: the crampons are iron spikes attached to a character's boots, providing better footing on ice or other slippery surfaces (the climbing seam).

bools.name: dnetDrillBore
bools.comment: the iron drill slowly bores through wooden or stone barriers, with a grinding noise audible up to 120 feet.

bools.name: dnetGrapplingHooks
bools.comment: the grappling hooks are two- or three-pronged hooks thrown at a catchable surface, nearly always with a rope attached (the climbing seam).

bools.name: dnetLanternShielded
bools.comment: the waterproof lantern produces light equivalent to a normal lantern, its flame carefully shielded against water dousing and gusts of wind.

bools.name: dnetLanternUwDouseByAir
bools.comment: underwater the illumination shrinks to a 10-foot radius; water does not extinguish the flame, but lack of air soon does - the DM makes the secret d6 roll for the rounds it continues to burn.

bools.name: dnetLardLubricant
bools.comment: lard is occasionally employed as a lubricant to help large objects, including characters, squeeze through small holes; it is mildly flammable but burns too stubbornly to function as a weapon.

bools.name: dnetLardInsulator
bools.comment: lard can also serve as an insulating coating for swimmers entering very cold water - see the hypothermia rules (page 42) for exact effects (the R516 seam).

bools.name: dnetOilSources
bools.comment: waterproofing oil is harvested from creatures with very effective insulation systems - seals and minks are common sources; cotton cannot be effectively waterproofed.

bools.name: dnetPickMinerKit
bools.comment: the pickaxe is an essential ingredient of every miner's kit, required for full excavation efficiency; in desperate conditions it can serve as a weapon with the nonproficiency penalties plus the inherent unwieldiness penalty.

bools.name: dnetChalkUses
bools.comment: the chalk powder serves a wide variety of purposes limited only by imagination: scattered on the floor it shows footprints, and hurled or smashed it creates a dust cloud settling on creatures in the area - discovering invisible creatures and lightening dark objects.

bools.name: dnetPulleyLoops
bools.comment: pulleys come with a wooden block and sturdy hooks; standard pulleys accept one loop of rope, others two or even three loops, and a single pulley changes the direction of force - very solid attachment required.

bools.name: dnetReedBreathing
bools.comment: the hollow reed is a slender straw that, used carefully, lets a character breathe completely submerged - inserted in the mouth with the nose sealed, lying on the back with the straw up like a small periscope.

bools.name: dnetReedHardToHide
bools.comment: the upside-down position makes concealment while moving very difficult, and moving risks the tell-tale ripple; simply floating with the current entails no such risk.

bools.name: dnetShovelMinerKit
bools.comment: the shovel is another standard item of every miner's supplies (the R520 seam).

bools.name: dnetWhistleSimple
bools.comment: the whistle is a simple device of hollowed wood, bone, or reed with a piercing sound audible up to 1,000 feet away.

bools.name: dnetBoatBackpack
bools.comment: the collapsible boat's skin hull and folding-spar frame fold into a backpack-sized package (filling the backpack), unfolding into a shallow boat equivalent to a small rowboat.

bools.name: dnetCanoeLight
bools.comment: the canoe is designed for light loads and easy paddling - much swifter and more maneuverable than a rowboat, but more susceptible to capsizing.

bools.name: dnetKayakSealed
bools.comment: the one-character kayak works well in rough or cold water, its oilskin layer completely surrounding the frame except the kayaker's opening - even capsizing does not fill it with water.
